audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for imitation, head/source/order, praying/prophesying, mutuality in Lord, Lord's supper abuse, discerning body.

verses.restored: Become imitators of me, just as I also am of Messiah.

familiar.text: Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.

modern.text: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.

original.text: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: I praise you because you remember me in all things and hold fast the traditions just as I handed them over to you.

familiar.text: Now I praise you, brethren, that ye remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.

modern.text: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.

original.text: Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ⸀ὑμᾶς ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις κατέχετε.

verses.restored: But I want you to know that the head/source of every man is Messiah, and head/source of woman is man, and head/source of Messiah is the Divine.

familiar.text: But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.

modern.text: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

original.text: θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ ἀνήρ, κεφαλὴ δὲ ⸀τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ θεός.

verses.restored: Every man praying or prophesying having something down over the head dishonors his head/source.

familiar.text: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonoureth his head.

modern.text: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.

original.text: πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: But every woman praying or prophesying with uncovered head dishonors her head/source; for it is one and the same as having been shaved.

familiar.text: But every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with her head uncovered dishonoureth her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven.

modern.text: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.

original.text: πᾶσα δὲ γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν ⸀αὐτῆς, ἓν γάρ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ.

verses.restored: For if a woman is not covered, let her also be shorn; but if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be covered.

familiar.text: For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered.

modern.text: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ οὐ κατακαλύπτεται γυνή, καὶ κειράσθω· εἰ δὲ αἰσχρὸν γυναικὶ τὸ κείρασθαι ἢ ξυρᾶσθαι, κατακαλυπτέσθω.

verses.restored: For a man indeed ought not cover the head, being image and glory of the Divine; but woman is glory of man.

familiar.text: For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.

modern.text: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

original.text: ἀνὴρ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ὀφείλει κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν, εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα θεοῦ ὑπάρχων· ⸀ἡ γυνὴ δὲ δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν.

verses.restored: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;

familiar.text: For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.

modern.text: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.

original.text: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ἐκ γυναικός, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ ἐξ ἀνδρός·

verses.restored: for also man was not created because of the woman, but woman because of the man.

familiar.text: Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.

modern.text: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.

original.text: καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα.

verses.restored: Because of this the woman ought to have authority upon her head, because of the messengers.

familiar.text: For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.

modern.text: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο ὀφείλει ἡ γυνὴ ἐξουσίαν ἔχειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους.

verses.restored: Nevertheless, neither woman apart from man nor man apart from woman in the Lord.

familiar.text: Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.

modern.text: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.

original.text: πλὴν οὔτε ⸂γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς⸃ ἐν κυρίῳ·

verses.restored: For just as the woman is from the man, so also the man is through the woman; but all things are from the Divine.

familiar.text: For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God.

modern.text: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.

original.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρός, οὕτως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ διὰ τῆς γυναικός· τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Judge among yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to the Divine uncovered?

familiar.text: Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered?

modern.text: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

original.text: ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς κρίνατε· πρέπον ἐστὶν γυναῖκα ἀκατακάλυπτον τῷ θεῷ προσεύχεσθαι;

verses.restored: Does not nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is dishonor to him,

familiar.text: Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?

modern.text: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,

original.text: ⸀οὐδὲ ⸂ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ⸃ διδάσκει ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἀνὴρ μὲν ἐὰν κομᾷ, ἀτιμία αὐτῷ ἐστιν,

verses.restored: but if a woman has long hair, it is glory to her? For the hair has been given to her instead of a covering.

familiar.text: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.

modern.text: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.

original.text: γυνὴ δὲ ἐὰν κομᾷ, δόξα αὐτῇ ἐστιν; ὅτι ἡ κόμη ἀντὶ περιβολαίου ⸀δέδοται.

verses.restored: But if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the assemblies of the Divine.

familiar.text: But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.

modern.text: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God. Sharing in the Lord’s Supper (Matthew 26:20–30; Mark 14:17–26; Luke 22:14–23)

original.text: εἰ δέ τις δοκεῖ φιλόνεικος εἶναι, ἡμεῖς τοιαύτην συνήθειαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, οὐδὲ αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: But in commanding this, I do not praise, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.

familiar.text: Now in this that I declare unto you I praise you not, that ye come together not for the better, but for the worse.

modern.text: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.

original.text: Τοῦτο δὲ ⸂παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ⸃ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε.

verses.restored: For first, when you come together in assembly, I hear there are splits among you, and in part I trust it.

familiar.text: For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it.

modern.text: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

original.text: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω.

verses.restored: For it is necessary that factions also be among you, so that the approved ones may become manifest among you.

familiar.text: For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.

modern.text: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.

original.text: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι, ἵνα ⸀καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: When you therefore come together in the same place, it is not to eat the Lord's supper.

familiar.text: When ye come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lord’s supper.

modern.text: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.

original.text: συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν,

verses.restored: For each one takes one's own supper beforehand in the eating, and one is hungry while another is drunk.

familiar.text: For in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken.

modern.text: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.

original.text: ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν, καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ, ὃς δὲ μεθύει.

verses.restored: Do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the assembly of the Divine and shame those having nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise.

familiar.text: What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.

modern.text: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!

original.text: μὴ γὰρ οἰκίας οὐκ ἔχετε εἰς τὸ ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν; ἢ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ καταφρονεῖτε, καὶ καταισχύνετε τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας; τί ⸂εἴπω ὑμῖν⸃; ἐπαινέσω ὑμᾶς; ἐν τούτῳ οὐκ ἐπαινῶ.

verses.restored: For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you, that the Lord Jesus, in the night he was handed over, took bread,

familiar.text: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread:

modern.text: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread,

original.text: Ἐγὼ γὰρ παρέλαβον ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ὃ καὶ παρέδωκα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ᾗ ⸀παρεδίδετο ἔλαβεν ἄρτον

verses.restored: and giving thanks, broke it and said, This is my body, which is for you; do this into my remembrance.

familiar.text: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.

modern.text: and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”

original.text: καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸀εἶπεν· Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

verses.restored: Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, as often as you drink, into my remembrance.

familiar.text: After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.

modern.text: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”

original.text: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, ὁσάκις ⸀ἐὰν πίνητε, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

verses.restored: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes.

familiar.text: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.

modern.text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

original.text: ὁσάκις γὰρ ⸀ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ⸀ποτήριον πίνητε, τὸν θάνατον τοῦ κυρίου καταγγέλλετε, ἄχρι ⸀οὗ ἔλθῃ.

verses.restored: Therefore whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will be liable concerning the body and blood of the Lord.

familiar.text: Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

modern.text: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.

original.text: Ὥστε ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ⸀ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ κυρίου ⸀ἀναξίως, ἔνοχος ἔσται τοῦ σώματος καὶ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ κυρίου.

verses.restored: Let a human examine oneself, and thus let one eat from the bread and drink from the cup.

familiar.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.

modern.text: Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.

original.text: δοκιμαζέτω δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἑαυτόν, καὶ οὕτως ἐκ τοῦ ἄρτου ἐσθιέτω καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου πινέτω·

verses.restored: For the one eating and drinking eats and drinks judgment to oneself if not discerning the body.

familiar.text: For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body.

modern.text: For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ ἐσθίων καὶ ⸀πίνων κρίμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει μὴ διακρίνων τὸ ⸀σῶμα.

verses.restored: Because of this many among you are weak and sick, and a considerable number sleep.

familiar.text: For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.

modern.text: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν ὑμῖν πολλοὶ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ἄρρωστοι καὶ κοιμῶνται ἱκανοί.

verses.restored: But if we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.

familiar.text: For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.

modern.text: Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.

original.text: εἰ ⸀δὲ ἑαυτοὺς διεκρίνομεν, οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα·

verses.restored: But being judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we may not be condemned with the world.

familiar.text: But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world.

modern.text: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.

original.text: κρινόμενοι δὲ ⸀ὑπὸ κυρίου παιδευόμεθα, ἵνα μὴ σὺν τῷ κόσμῳ κατακριθῶμεν.

verses.restored: So then, my siblings, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

familiar.text: Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, tarry one for another.

modern.text: So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

original.text: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, συνερχόμενοι εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν ἀλλήλους ἐκδέχεσθε.

verses.restored: If anyone is hungry, let that one eat at home, so that you may not come together into judgment. The remaining things I will set in order when I come.

familiar.text: And if any man hunger, let him eat at home; that ye come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come.

modern.text: If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.

original.text: ⸀εἴ τις πεινᾷ, ἐν οἴκῳ ἐσθιέτω, ἵνα μὴ εἰς κρίμα συνέρχησθε. Τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ὡς ἂν ἔλθω διατάξομαι.

translation_notes: Kephale is rendered head/source to preserve the debated range of headship/source/order language.
Women are explicitly praying and prophesying in the assembly; the issue is ordered honor, not silencing.
Discerning the body includes the communal body, especially the poor shamed at the meal.
